[LERR.9.5] **Latched per site.** Both schemas are `scope internal` ([LSCP.2.6]), and
the engine applies one replacement rule of its own when it asserts a fault fact.
Before asserting, it **must** look for a live fault fact of the same schema with
the same `(node, rule)`:

- if every slot is equal, the assertion is a suppressed no-op, as a no-op
  reassertion is ([LFAC.2.5.1]) — the live fact stays, and nothing matching it
  fires again;
- if any slot differs, the engine retracts the live fact and asserts the new
  one ([LFAC.1.2.2]).

A rule acknowledges a fault by `withdraw`ing the fact it matched
([LSCP.2.6.1]); the next fault at that site is then asserted afresh. The
replacement rule belongs to fault facts alone: it is not a property of any
scope, `internal` included.

So working memory holds at most one fault fact per schema per `(node, rule)`
site, a bound the compiler knows from the artefact ([LERR.9.10]). The event trace
still records every occurrence ([LERR.9.1]).
